label: LLM self-feedback (5 loops)
info:
DEVELOPER SAMPLE: an Agent-mode self-feedback loop with Auto deploy enabled.

Each iteration = one LLM request + one live canvas edit + one automatic Deploy, so the loop is HARD-CAPPED AT 5 ITERATIONS via the ?loop= query parameter. Do not remove the guard — an unbounded loop would keep consuming your LLM API and keep deploying.

SETUP (all three steps matter):
1. Set a model on the 'LLM (agent, auto deploy)' node (or configure one in the sidebar).
2. In the editor's Deploy button dropdown, select 'Modified Flows' (or 'Modified Nodes') BEFORE running. A 'Full' deploy restarts EVERY flow — including this loop flow — which discards the message waiting in the 5 s delay and kills the loop after one iteration. That is also why the LLM's edit target (the 'feedback_log' comment) lives on the separate 'LLM feedback target' tab: with Modified Flows, only that tab restarts and this loop keeps running.
3. Keep exactly ONE editor window open. Every open editor applies and auto-deploys, and multiple editors will conflict.

HOW IT WORKS:
- Click the inject button. It calls GET /llm-loop?loop=1 on this instance.
- The 'http in' endpoint acknowledges immediately, then asks the LLM (Agent mode) to update ONLY the 'feedback_log' comment on the 'LLM feedback target' tab.
- The open editor applies the change and auto-deploys (developer feature).
- After a 5 s settle delay, the flow calls /llm-loop?loop=N+1 — until loop 5.
- Any error (missing model, unreachable URL, LLM failure) is surfaced by the 'loop errors' catch node instead of dying silently.

The loop URL defaults to http://127.0.0.1:1880. If your Node-RED listens elsewhere (e.g. embedded at :8000/red), set the environment variable LLM_LOOP_BASE (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8000/red) — it is read in the single 'next loop URL' function node.
